name: bigbang
author: LLM, from the human's big-bang scenario (2026-07-18). Research-pinned architecture facts, never taste. Serves BOTH twins (core/trainables/bigbang.py CPU, bigbang_gpu.py GPU) - same fact names.
scenario: The metaphorical big bang: seed a spinning 3D cloud of matter parcels (INITIAL CONDITIONS: spin, flatten0 - where all authorship lives once the law is fixed), run one uniform law (softened gravity + inelastic mergers + torque-free gas circularization - the SHORTCUTS that compress un-simulable megayears into the budget), and demand the settled result be a SOLAR SYSTEM in the researched, architecture-level sense: one dominant central mass, a handful of planets on nearly-circular, nearly-coplanar orbits obeying an EMPIRICALLY MEASURED Kepler third law, with the giant-impact era over. Reality pins: the Sun holds 99.86 percent of the solar system's mass; 8 planets; T^2 proportional to a^3 (Kepler 1619, measured here as the log T vs log a slope of the grown orbits - the law is never coded, it must emerge); 6 of 8 planets have e < 0.1 (Mercury's 0.206 is the outlier); planetary inclinations to the invariable plane are a few degrees (Mercury 6.3 the outlier); formation simulations routinely eject substantial planetesimal mass. Scale honesty: N0=96 equal-mass parcels cannot reproduce Sun:Mercury = 6e6 mass ratios or Myr timescales - every anchor here is an ARCHITECTURE fact, not an absolute mass or age.

constraints.why: THE PHYSICS RECEIPT, HARD: pairwise central forces and radial-only drag are exactly torque-free about z, mergers bank their internal angular momentum in a spin ledger, escapees in a removal ledger - so L_z(alive)+L_z(spin)+L_z(removed) vs L_z(t0) measures ONLY floating-point error and bookkeeping sins. The ledger already caught one structural bug (stale post-merge forces: drift 0.527 on the first CPU smoke). Measured fp32 GPU floor: 8.4e-6 over 10k steps with ~90 mergers; the wall sits 6x above it. A universe that leaks angular momentum is not simulating gravity.

A STAR MUST DOMINATE, not merely form: the Sun holds 99.86 percent of the solar system's mass, and dominance is not cosmetic - it is what makes MULTIPLE planets possible. Run-2 lesson (objective iteration, never artifact): with the floor at 0.55 the optimizer parked at 0.579, leaving 42 percent of the mass to accrete into 1-2 STELLAR COMPANIONS whose Hill spheres spanned half the disk - one sweeper, no system, Kepler term never engaged. At 0.85+ the leftover is <= 15 percent, each planet a few percent, Hill isolation holds, and a multi-planet architecture is physically reachable at N0=96. Original floor rationale (kill failed collapses like the smoke seed's 0.36) is strictly contained in the new floor.

A SYSTEM, NOT A BINARY - on the WORST restart. Floor raised 2 -> 3 after run 2: the empirical-Kepler fit needs 3 or more measurable planets, and with the floor at 2 the band paid 0.94 satisfaction at ONE planet, hiding the Kepler cliff from the gradient entirely. Now the planet-count pressure and the Kepler requirement point the same way. Ceiling unchanged: a dozen-body debris swarm is not planets.
Gradient shaping toward the multi-planet regime (mean across restarts) so the search feels progress between the integer jumps the worst-case band moves in.

THE LAW MUST EMERGE: Kepler's third law (1619) - T^2 proportional to a^3, slope 1.5 in log-log - measured EMPIRICALLY from each grown system's orbits (winding-accumulated periods vs mean radii; nothing in the simulation states it). Hitting this band requires the system to have actually become star-dominated and near-integrable: planets on independent Keplerian orbits with negligible cross-perturbation. The +/-0.2 tolerance covers finite eccentricity and the few-planet fit. A 0.0 (fewer than 3 measurable planets) fails the band, coupling this term to planet formation itself.

The Kepler fit must be a LAW, not a coincidence of scatter: log T vs log a must be tight (r^2 >= 0.85) on every restart's worst fit. Guards against a slope that lands near 1.5 by averaging wild residuals.

ACCRETION CIRCULARIZES: 6 of 8 real planets have e < 0.1 (Mercury's 0.206 is the famous outlier). A median above 0.2 means the gas shortcut and the merger history failed to damp the orbits - a system of crossing ellipses is a demolition derby, not an architecture.

THE DISK MUST EMERGE: real planetary inclinations to the invariable plane are a few degrees (Mercury 6.3 the outlier). The cloud starts 3D (flatten0 up to a raw sphere); flattening into a common plane is angular-momentum physics the genome cannot fake - rms inclination of the grown planets vs the system's own total-L plane must land in the researched range.

SETTLED ARCHITECTURE: the giant-impact era must be OVER by sim end - at most 2 mergers in the final 20 percent of any restart. A system still eating itself has not reached its attractor; the game world plays inside the settled result.

Ejection is real formation physics (scattering tosses planetesimals out; the solar system did plenty) but a law that flings half the cloud past 50 length units has chosen explosion over accretion. Loose wall, mostly a degeneracy guard.

THE CLIMBING TERM (a spec made only of walls gets you exactly the walls): of the mass that neither fell into the star nor escaped, how much got PACKED into actual planets (>= 3 parcels, bound) - accretion completeness, worst restart. ref=0.3 sits near the smoke seed's 0.32 so there is real room to climb, and climbing is resisted by the ecc and late-merger walls: aggressive accretion pumps eccentricity and keeps the impact era running. The tension is the design.
